name: TSC complex subunit 2
pathways: regulation of small GTPase mediated signal transduction

function.text: TSC2 encodes tuberin. Annotated molecular activities include GTPase activator activity and protein homodimerization activity. It participates in small GTPase-mediated signal transduction and regulation of small GTPase mediated signal transduction.

germline.text: Strong or definitive GenCC assertions link constitutional variants to tuberous sclerosis 2 (autosomal dominant).

somatic.text: Reported somatic alteration contexts include PEComa, malignant; Pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor; Eosinophilic solid and cystic renal cell carcinoma. The alteration class and exact variant must be assessed in the disease context.

function.text: TSC2 encodes tuberin. Based in part on similarity, it is the catalytic component of the TSC-TBC complex, a multiprotein complex that acts as a negative regulator of the canonical mTORC1 complex, an evolutionarily conserved central nutrient sensor that stimulates anabolic reactions and macromolecule biosynthesis to promote cellular biomass generation and growth. The TSC-TBC complex is inactivated in response to nutrients, relieving inhibition of mTORC1. It participates in microtubule-mediated protein transport via its ability to regulate mTORC1 signaling.

germline.text: Pathogenic germline variants are associated with tuberous sclerosis 2 (autosomal dominant).

somatic.text: Somatic alterations involving TSC2 have been reported in PEComa, malignant, pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor, and eosinophilic solid and cystic renal cell carcinoma.
